references.authors: Giovannoni G, Boyko A, Correale J, Edan G, Freedman MS, Montalban X, et al
references.title: Long-term follow-up of patients with a first clinical demyelinating event (clinically isolated syndrome) who received cladribine tablets in CLASSIC-MS: findings for the ORACLE-MS cohort

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
• Study design: CLASSIC-MS observational, ambispective, long-term, low-interventional, multicenter, phase IV.
  • Parent trials: CLARITY and CLARITY Extension (patients previously treated and then followed up).
  • Follow-up: median 13.1 years from last dose in parent trial (range 11.4–16.2).

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
• Total: 435 patients.
  • Median age at CLASSIC-MS: 55 years (range 34–82).
  • Sex: 68.3% female.
  • Disease course: RRMS 71.7%, SPMS 28.3%.
  • Median disease duration: 24 years.
  • Median EDSS at CLASSIC-MS baseline: 4.0 (vs 2.5 at CLARITY baseline).
  • 398 patients previously exposed to cladribine; 37 placebo only .

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
• Parent trials: cladribine tablets (cumulative dose typically 3.5 mg/kg over 2 years) vs placebo.
  • CLASSIC-MS: non-interventional long-term follow-up, no additional trial treatment.
  • Information collected: subsequent DMT use, relapses, disability progression .

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcome

  • Long-term mobility: proportion of patients not requiring a wheelchair (not wheelchair-bound or bedridden, EDSS <7).

Secondary outcomes

  • Long-term disability: proportion of patients not requiring an ambulatory aid (EDSS <6).
  • Relapse activity (annualized relapse rate, time to first relapse).
  • Use of subsequent DMTs (proportion never starting another DMT, time to next therapy).
  • Employment status (proportion employed at follow-up).
  • Mortality.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value:
• Conflicts of interest: multiple authors with pharma industry ties, including Merck.
  • Funding: Merck Healthcare KGaA.
  • We emailed the corresponding author (Prof. Gavin Giovannoni) to request data on the number of participants free from disability worsening at 24 months after randomisation and at the end of follow-up, but he informed us that these data were not available.

risk-of-bias.domain: Bias arising from the randomization process
risk-of-bias.support-for-judgement: No re-randomization or allocation concealment occurred in CLASSIC-MS; follow-up cohorts were defined by prior exposure (‘cladribine-exposed’ vs ‘never-exposed’) among a post-randomization subset of the parent trials. Hence, baseline comparability from the original randomization is unlikely to be preserved, leading to high risk of bias in the randomization domain.

references.authors: Spelman T, Ozakbas S, Alroughani R, Terzi M, Hodgkinson S, Laureys G, et al
references.title: Comparative effectiveness of cladribine tablets versus other oral disease-modifying treatments for multiple sclerosis: results from MSBase registry

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
• Design: Retrospective observational study using prospectively collected data, based on the international MSBase registry (31 countries). Comparison between oral DMT cohorts.
  • Eligibility: pwMS who initiated/re-initiated cladribine, fingolimod, dimethyl fumarate, or teriflunomide from 2018 to mid-2021; ≥18 years; ≥12 months of pre-index data; >6 months of follow-up; minimum dataset for propensity score. Excluded: active/recent pregnancy, other demyelinating diseases, malignancy. Each patient contributed to only one treatment cohort; index = treatment start date. Censoring at treatment switch/discontinuation, death, loss to follow-up, pregnancy, or study end.
  • Statistical analysis: propensity score matching (1:1, cladribine vs comparator), balance defined as standardized difference <0.15; pairwise censoring applied; Kaplan–Meier survival curves; Cox models (proportional hazards tested with Schoenfeld residuals); analyses conducted in Stata 16.1.
  • Observed follow-up: median (IQR): cladribine 1.14 years (0.49–1.92), fingolimod 1.28 (0.57–2.01), dimethyl fumarate 0.97 (0.36–1.80), teriflunomide 1.10 (0.50–1.95).

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
• Total: 3,475 patients.
  • Treatment groups: cladribine (633), fingolimod (1,195), natalizumab (1,649), alemtuzumab (481), ocrelizumab (512).
  • Baseline characteristics: mean age across cohorts 36.9–44.1 years; >70% female in each cohort; mean disease duration 6.8–12.5 years; mean relapses in prior 12 months 0.5–0.7; proportion treatment-naïve 13.9%–46.3%.

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
• Real-world oral DMTs:
    • Cladribine tablets (MAVENCLAD®)
    • Fingolimod (GILENYA®)
    • Dimethyl fumarate (TECFIDERA®)
    • Teriflunomide (AUBAGIO®)
  • No experimental procedures; follow-up was observational only.

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
• Primary endpoints:
    • Time to treatment switch
    • Time to discontinuation
  • Secondary endpoints:
    • Time to first relapse
    • Annualized relapse rate (ARR)

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value:
Funding and conflicts of interest: Supported by EMD Serono Research & Development Institute, Inc. (affiliated with Merck KGaA). Two authors employed by sponsor (NT, SLW); other authors disclosed ties with pharmaceutical companies.

We emailed the corresponding author (Prof. Tim Spelman) to request data on the number of patients experiencing a new relapse at the end of follow-up, and he provided the information.

references.authors: Montalban X, Leist TP, Cohen BA, Moses H, Campbell J, Hicking C, et al
references.title: Cladribine tablets added to IFN-β in active relapsing MS: the ONWARD study

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
Design: Randomised, phase IIb, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of add-on therapy with IFN-β and two different doses of oral cladribine.

Setting: Outpatient clinics.

Location: multicentre, 4 countries (US, Italy, Russian Federation, Spain), 50 centres .

The study period ran from November 2006 to March 2012

Sample size In April 2008, the high-dose cladribine add-on arm was discontinued due to a safety signal and the study design was amended accordingly.

  • Number of participants randomised 42
  • Number of participants who completed the study 36
  • Number of participantss who completed treatment 19

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
All patients were treated with IFN-ß, and all forms were allowed: 

  • IFN-β-1a, 44 μg SC 3 times weekly; 
  • IFN-β-1a, 30 μg IM once weekly;
  • IFN-β-1b, 250 μg SC every other day

Oral cladribine was administered at two cumulative doses (3.5 or 5.25 mg/kg bw).

 A course consisted of one or two 10 mg/kg of cladribine tablets given once daily for the first 4 cycles of a 28-day period. 

Placebo was administered on a similar schedule.

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcome: Safety and tolerability of oral cladribine added to IFN-β therapy

  • Treatment Emergent AEs (TEAEs) in the System Organ Class infections and infestations; 
  • Incidence of TEAEs and SAEs, including neoplasms; 
  • CTCAE grade 3 or 4 severity toxicity in haematology 
  • Liver function parameters; 
  • Time to first grade 3/4 haematologic or liver toxicity; time to recover from grade 3/4 haematologic or liver toxicity; 
  • Lymphocyte counts

Secondary outcome of the study was not powered for efficacy: 

  • Number of qualifying relapses over 96 weeks; time to first qualifying relapse; mean numbers of new Gd+ T1, active T2, and combined unique active lesions (new Gd+ T1, or new or enlarging T2 lesions, or both, without double counting) on MRI scans at 96 weeks; 
  • Time to confirm 3-month EDSS progression.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value:
Enrolment terminated because of haematologic toxicities (grade 3/4 lymphopenia) in the cladribine 5.25mg/kg+IFN-β arm. This resulted in a change in the randomisation schema, number of patients and planned population analyses.

Participants continued only IFN-ß and were followed up for safety (USA population). 

Supported by Merck Serono SA Geneva, Switzerland, a subsidiary of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Patient characteristics in the original and amended protocol:

  • Gender: 69.7% women, 30.3% men  
  • Race 96% white
  • Age means 39.6 years
  • EDSS mean score: 2.9
  • Disease duration: mean 9.5 years
  • Previous therapy of any DMDs: 100% 
  • Subtype of MS: RR 90.5%, SR 9.5%
  • MRI lesions Gd+ T1: mean per patient 0.9

Inclusion Criteria: RRMS or SPMS (2005 McDonald criteria) with ≥ 1 MS relapse while receiving treatment with IFN-β for ≥48 consecutive weeks before screening, EDSS score of 1.0–5.5, clinical stability during 28 days before screening, normal haematologic parameters within 28 days of baseline.

Exclusion Criteria: 

Infectious or immune-compromising diseases, 

  • Past or present malignancies, amended to exclude basal cell skin cancer, 
  • History or evidence of tuberculosis, 
  • Previous treatment with immunosuppressive or cytotoxic therapies at any time, treatment with cytokine-based therapy or plasmaphaeresis within 3 months of baseline, treatment with adrenocorticotropic hormone within 28 days of baseline. 
  • Pregnancy, breastfeeding, attempting conception, refusal to use contraception during study (men and women), amended to include use of contraception for 6 months after the last dose of study drug in women. 
  • Treatment with oral or parenteral corticosteroids within 28 days of baseline or within 30 days of screening, 
  • Treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin therapy within 3 months of baseline or within 30 days of screening.

risk-of-bias.domain: Bias arising from the randomization process
risk-of-bias.support-for-judgement:
This study is made by two studies and the details on randomization are in the amended study. We consider what authors described in the amended study.
For some paramethers there are differences expressed in table1, but despite some differences observed at baseline in the demographics of the ONWARD study between the two subgroups, it should be noted that these differences were not meaningful.

references.title: Cladribine versus fingolimod, natalizumab and interferon β for multiple sclerosis

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
Design: Observational registries study comparing four MS cohorts (cladribine, fingolimod, IFN-β and natalizumab) analysed with propensity score-match

Setting: Outpatient clinic 

Location: people from The Australian Cladribine Product Familiarisation Program and from MSBase, WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform.

Study Period: 2011

Sample Size: 

  • Number of patients included in the cohorts: Cladribine 111, IFN-β 9286, Fingolimod 4843 and Natalizumab 4125
  • Number of patients available for matching: Cladribine 37, IFN-β 1940, Fingolimod 1892 and Natalizumab 1410
  • Number of patients retained in the 3 pairwise matched cohorts:
    • 22 Cladribine vs 167-IFN β
    • 32 Cladribine vs 258 Fingolimod
    • 26 Cladribine vs 174 Natalizumab

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Participants' characteristics: 

  • Gender: 76.6% women, 23.4% men
  • Race: NA
  • Age: 47.6 years (range from 44 years in natalizumab to 50 years in cladribine cohort)
  • EDSS median score: 3.8 (from 3.5 to 4.5)
  • Median Disease duration: 12.8 years (from 4.5 to 23.8)
  • Previous therapy with DMDs: 80% (in IFN-β group it was up to 92%)
  • Subtypes of MS: RRMS 84.8% with the highest percentage in the IFN-β group (90%) and the lowest in the cladribine group (75%), SPMS 15.2% with the highest percentage in the cladribine group (25%) and the lowest in the IFN-β group, 10%.
  • MRI lesion Gd+ T1: NA

Inclusion criteria: definite relapse-onset MS, exposure to one of the study therapies, continuous study monotherapy ⩾1 year, minimum required to be recorded follow-up (3 months prior to starting treatment and two disability scores ⩾6 months) and minimum dataset (consisting of sex, age, date of first MS symptom, dates of clinical relapses, clinical MS course and disability score at treatment commencement (−1 year to +1 month)).

Esclusion criteria: no prior exposure to alemtuzumab, mitoxantrone, rituximab or haematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
• Oral cladribine 3.5 mg/kg cumulative dose, initial treatment consisting of two courses completed in 2 weeks,
  • Subcutaneously IFN-β 1a 44 μg 3 times weekly
  • Oral fingolimod 0.5 mg daily
  • Intravenously natalizumab 300 μg every 4 weeks

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Outcome timing: defined by the inclusion of patients in the study that was over one year on-treatment follow-up. 

Primary outcomes: Proportion of patients free from relapses, disability accumulation events and disability improvement events while on study therapy.

references.authors: Giovannoni G, Soelberg Sorensen P, Cook S, Rammohan K, Rieckmann P, Comi G, et al
references.title: Safety and efficacy of cladribine tablets in patients with relapsing–remitting multiple sclerosis: results from the randomized extension trial of the CLARITY study

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
Design: phase IIIb, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group, extension trial

Setting: Outpatient clinic

Location: multicenter: countries 30 (Australia, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Latvia, Lebanon, Lithuania, Morocco, Poland, Portugal, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Serbia & Montenegro, Switzerland, Tunisia, Turkey, UK, Ukraine, USA), centres 133

Sample Size

  • Number of patients who completed Giovannoni 2010: 1184
  • Number of patients finally included in Giovannoni 2018: 806
  • Number of patients who completed Giovannoni 2018: 738

The study period started in January 2008 and ended in July 2009.

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Participants' characteristics:

  • Gender: 65.9% women, 34.2% man
  • Race: 97.6% white, 2.4% other
  • Age: mean 41 years, range 18-65
  • EDSS means score of 2.6 (range from 0 to 6.5)
  • Disease duration 11.1 years
  • Time gap between the two studies: 40.3 weeks expressed in mean 
  • Subtypes of MS: RR
  • Participants with MRI lesions Gd+T1: reported number and volume of Gd+ T1 lesions and T2 volume

Inclusion criteria: 

  • Patients who complete Giovannoni 2010
  • Normal haematological results within 28 days of the first planned dose. 

Patients who had received IFN-β or glatiramer acetate during the period between the two studies had to discontinue their DMD ⩾3 months before the first day of the Extension study.

Exclusion criteria: Participants who were not enroled in Giovannoni 2010

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Intervention

  • Patients who received placebo in the CLARITY study were assigned to cladribine tablets 3.5 mg/kg (this was the non-randomised arm of the study),
  • Patients treated with cladribine tablets in CLARITY were re-randomised (2:1) to cladribine tablets 3.5 mg/kg or placebo. This means that there were 5 other treatment groups in the study with different cumulative doses over the completed four years of treatment (CLARITY + CLARITY Extension):
    • Cladribine 3.5 mg/kg in CLARITY and placebo in CLARITY Extension;
    • Cladribine 5.25 mg/kg in CLARITY and placebo in CLARITY Extension;
    • Cladribine 3.5 mg/kg in CLARITY and cladribine tablets 3.5 mg/kg in CLARITY Extension for a total dose of 7 mg/kg;
    • Cladribine 5.25 mg/kg in CLARITY and cladribine tablets 3.5 mg/kg in CLARITY Extension for a total dose of 8.75 mg/kg;
    • Placebo in CLARITY and cladribine 3.5 mg/kg in CLARITY Extension for a total dose of 3.5 mg/kg

Placebo: In our analysis, we considered the people who received placebo in CLARITY study to be the placebo group.

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value: Clinical endpoints included the annualised relapse rate (ARR), proportion of patients free of qualifying relapses, time to first qualifying relapse, and time to confirmed EDSS progression.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value: Sponsored by EMD Serono, Inc., a business of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany (in the United States), and Merck Serono SA, Geneva, an affiliate of Merck KGaA Darmstadt, Germany (rest of the world). Data statistical analyses and medical writing support are funded by Merck KGaA, Darmstadt

risk-of-bias.domain: Bias arising from the randomization process
risk-of-bias.support-for-judgement:
In Extension study there were 5 arms; patients who received placebo in CLARITY received directly cladribine 3.5 mg/kg without any randomisation. Randomization in CLARITY Extension was stratified by CLARITY treatment. In fact "patients treated with cladribine ( 3.5 or 5.25 mg/Kg) in CLARITY were re-randomized (2:1) to cladribine 3.5 mg/kg or placebo". "The randomisation was centralised, using an interactive voice response system".
The characteristics of patients who entered the OLE were similar across groups at baseline, except those patients who received placebo in CLARITY. They showed evidence of greater disease activity (Table 1).

references.title: A placebo-controlled trial of oral cladribine for relapsing multiple sclerosis

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
Design: randomised, phase IIIb, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group

Setting: Outpatient clinic.

Location: multicenter: countries 32 (Australia, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Brazil, Canada, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Lebanon, Latvia, Lithuania, Marocco, The Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Serbia Montenegro, Switzerland, Tunisia, Turkey, UK, Ukraine, USA),clinical centres 155

The study period started in April 2005 and ran for two years, to January 2007. Follow-up lasted 96 weeks

Sample Size

  • Number of participants randomised: 1326
  • Number of participants who completed the study: 1184

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Participants' characteristics:

  • Gender: 67.7% women, 32.3% man 
  • Race: 98.1% white, 0.5% black, 1.4% other 
  • Age mean: 38.5 years, ranging from 18 to 65
  • EDSS means score: 2.9
  • Disease Duration 8.7 years (range from 0.4 to 42.3)
  • Previous therapy of any DMD: 30.3% 
  • Subtypes of MS: RR
  • MRI lesions Gd+ T1: 31.1% patients at baseline

Inclusion criteria: RRMS according to McDonald criteria 2001, lesions consistent with MS on MRI according to Fazekas criteria 1988, one relapse within 12 months prior to study entry, EDSS ⋜ 5.5. A washout period of at least 3 months prior to study entry was required if the patient had received a DMD.

Exclusion criteria: Abnormal haematological test results < 28 days prior to study entry, condition that could compromise immune function, relapse < 28 days prior to study entry, failure of two or more DMDs, or immunosuppressive therapy at any time before study entry or, < 3 months had received cytokine-based therapy, intravenous immunoglobulin therapy, or plasmaphaeresis.

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Intervention cumulative dose of oral cladribine 3.5 mg/kg or 5.25 mg/kg b/w. A course consisted of one or two 10 mg cladribine tablets given once daily for the first 4 or 5 days of a 28-day period.  

In the first 48-week period, treatment was given in two or four courses during the first 48 weeks (weeks 1, 5, 9, 13). Patients in the 3.5 mg group received 2 courses of cladribine followed by 2 courses of placebo; patients in the 5.25 mg group received 4 courses of cladribine or 4 courses of placebo.  

In the second 48-week period, patients in both cladribine groups received 2 courses of cladribine and the placebo group received 2 courses of placebo, starting at weeks 48 and 52 (8 to 10 days of treatment).

Placebo: One or two tablets on a similar schedule.

Use of additional intervention: rescue therapy with subcutaneous IFN-β 1a (at a dose of 44 μg three times per week).

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcome: Rate of relapse at 96 weeks.

Secondary outcome: 

  • Proportion of patients who were relapse-free,
  • Time to sustained progression of disability measured by EDSS,
  • Time to the first relapse,
  • Proportion of patients receiving rescue therapy with INF-β 1a,
  • MRI end points at 96 weeks (mean number of lesions per patient per scan for Gd+ T1 lesions, active T2-weighted lesions, and combined unique lesions).

Safety end points: incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events; physical examination; laboratory measurements.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value: Supported by Merck Serono, with analyses of data, in accordance with the statistical plan. Editorial assistance was provided by Acumed, which was funded by Merck Serono.

risk-of-bias.domain: Bias arising from the randomization process
risk-of-bias.support-for-judgement:
"Randomisation was performed with the use of a central system and a computer-generated treatment randomisation code, with dynamic allocation by site in permuted blocks of six".
"The demographic and clinical characteristics of the ITT population were generally well-balanced across the three study groups, although patients receiving 3.5 mg of cladribine/Kg had a shorter significative mean duration of disease".

characteristics.name: Methods
characteristics.value:
Design randomised, phase III study, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group.

Setting Outpatient Clinics of hospitals, private clinics, or treatment centres

Location: multicentre: 34 countries (US, Argentina, Austria, Belgium, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Canada, Croatia, Czechia, Estonia, Finland, France, Georgia, Germany, India, Italy, Republic of Korea, Lebanon, Macedonia, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Russian Federation, Serbia, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom), 160 centres

Study period from 21 October 2008 to 11 October 2010. There was an early termination of the study in October 2011, at which time all cladribine administration was stopped.

Sample Size 

  • Number of participants: 616 
  • Number of participants who completed the study: 467
  • Number of participants who completed the six treatment courses: 363

characteristics.name: Participants
characteristics.value:
Characteristics of the participants:

  • Gender: 65% women, 35% men
  • Race 94% White, <1%, Black, 5% Asian, <1% Other

  • Patients with previous therapy of any DMDs: Not applicable
  • Participants with Gd+ T1 MRI lesion : median number 0 (0.0-1.0)
  • Use of steroid treatment: 66%

Inclusion criteria 

  • First clinical demyelinating event (mono or poly symptomatic) within 75 days before screening, showed at least two clinically silent lesions of at least 3 mm on a T2-weighted brain MRI, at least one of which was ovoid, periventricular, or infratentorial
  • EDSS ≤ 5.0. 

Exclusion criteria 

  • Diagnosis of MS (McDonald 2005) or any other disease that could better explain the patient’s initial symptoms, 
  • History or evidence of latent or active tuberculosis. 
  • Pregnant or breastfeeding woman, or not willing to use contraception throughout the study and for 90 days after the last dose of study drug.

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Intervention:

Oral Cladribine total cumulative dose 3.5 mg/kg: received cladribine 0·875 mg/kg per course for two courses, plus placebo for two courses during the first 48 weeks, then two courses of cladribine 0·875 mg/kg during the second 48 weeks. 

Oral Cladribine total cumulative dose 5.25 mg/Kg: received cladribine 0·875 mg/kg per course for four courses during the first 48 weeks, then two courses during the second 48 weeks.

Treatment courses were scheduled during year 1 on day 1 and weeks 5, 9, and 13, and during year 2 in weeks 48 and 52. Every course was given over 4 or 5 consecutive days, with 10 mg of cladribine tablets.

Placebo: oral tablets for four courses of treatment during the first 48 weeks, then two courses during the second 48 weeks.

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary end point: Time to conversion to clinically definite MS (Poser criteria) during the double-blind treatment period

Secondary end points: 

  • Time to conversion to MS (McDonald 2005) during the double-blind treatment period  
  • Number of new or persisting T1 Gd+ lesions, new or enlarging T2 lesions, combined unique active lesions over 96 weeks (or up to the last available scan), percentage change from baseline in brain volume, volume of T1 Gd+ lesions and T2 lesions over time, proportions of patients free from new T1 Gd+ lesions and new or enlarging T2 lesions, numbers of T1 hypo intense.   

Safety end points: Adverse events, serious adverse events, vital signs, laboratory variables, concomitant medications and procedures.

characteristics.name: Notes
characteristics.value:
a. Patients converting to CDMS entered the Open-label maintenance treatment (OLMT) and received subcutaneous IFN-β 1a, 44 μg three times weekly. 
b. Patients not converting to CDMS entered Long-term follow-up (LFU) They were without study drugs until conversion, when they were treated with open-label cladribine 3·5 mg/kg under the original design, or with subcutaneous IFN-β 1a, 44 μg three times weekly after early trial termination (amendment due to the sponsor’s decision).

Data was collected, analysed, and interpreted by the sponsor, Merck Serono SA Geneva, Switzerland, a subsidiary of Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany.

risk-of-bias.domain: Bias arising from the randomization process

"Randomisation was done using a central web-based randomisation system and was stratified by geographic region. Masking was maintained nusing a two-physician model (both doctors were masked)".
"Baseline patient demographics and disease characteristics were well balanced across treatment groups".

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Intervention: Cladribine infused through a central venous catheter using a portable pump. A cumulative dose of 2.8 mg of cladribine x kg, b/w. Four courses for 4 months, each course was of 7 days of treatment, each day was 0.10 mg per kg for a total of cladribine at 0.7 mg/kg per course. 

2nd year: people treated with cladribine crossed over to placebo.

Placebo: participants who had received placebo were given active drug, but at one-half the total dose that had been administered during the first year (1.4 mg/kg)

Supplementary intervention participants were permitted to continue medication to treat some symptoms of MS.

Design: Randomised, phase III double-blind, crossover study. Only the first phase (one year) of the crossover study was considered.

risk-of-bias.domain: Bias arising from the randomization process
risk-of-bias.support-for-judgement: Initially, 24 pairs of patients "were matched for age, gender and disease severity". Each matched pair "was randomised by the statistician using random number tables, so that one patient was assigned to the cladribine group and the other to the placebo group" (we do not know which patient started treatment first, number 1 or 2). In our opinion, this mechanism was biased. In addition, the authors replaced 2 patients lost to FU initially attributed to cladribine without considering their pairs with placebo. Demographic characteristics of patients at baseline are shown in Table 1.

Inclusion criteria Clinically definite MS according to the Schumacher criteria or Poser criteria (chronic slow progression of signs and symptoms) over the preceding 12 or 24 months; EDSS score between 3.0 and 6.5; age 21 to 60 years; serum creatinine levels 1.5 mg/dL and creatinine clearance 80% of age-adjusted normal value; aspartate and alanine transaminase and alkaline phosphatase levels less than twice the normal upper limit; neutrophil count 1600/mL and platelet count 130,000/mL; clinically normal ECG and chest x-ray.

Exclusion criteria Significant history of medical disease within the preceding 2 years; use of corticosteroids or other immunosuppressants or IFN-β within the preceding 3 months; total lymphoid irradiation; persistent leukopenia or thrombocytopenia after treatment with immuno suppressive agents; history of alcohol or drug abuse within the preceding year or of attempted suicide; malignancy or history of malignancy within the preceding 5 years; pregnancy or nursing; positive test result for HIV; use of an experimental drug or device within the preceding 60 days; or prior participation in a trial with cladribine.

characteristics.name: Interventions
characteristics.value:
Patients were assigned to one of three treatment groups (subcutaneous cladribine 2.1 mg/kg, subcutaneous cladribine 0.7 mg/kg; or placebo).

Six courses of cladribine 0.07 mg/kg/day SC for 5 consecutive days (total dose, 2.1 mg/kg), followed by two courses of placebo or two courses of cladribine 0.07 mg/kg/day SC for 5 consecutive days (total dose, 0.7 mg/kg), followed by six courses of placebo or eight courses of placebo SC for 5 consecutive
days.

Concomitant therapy. 

  • Methylprednisolone, 1 g/day for up to 5 days, was allowed only for treatment of severe exacerbations.
  • Symptomatic therapies to treat troublesome symptoms were allowed.

characteristics.name: Outcomes
characteristics.value:
Primary outcome: means change in EDSS and SNRS scores from baseline to the final evaluation during the 12-month double-blind phase.

Secondary outcome: 

  • Mean change from baseline in SNRS score and time to progression of MS.
  • Adverse Events, most common treatment-emergent adverse events, haematologic changes, serum chemistry.
  • Proportion of participants with enhanced T1 lesions, volume and number of enhanced T1 lesions.
  • Adverse Event and Treatment Emergent Adverse Event, Clinical laboratory analysis and Physical Findings

"Patients were assigned to one of three parallel treatment groups according to a computer-generated randomization schedule stratifyed by baseline disease severity and site".
We believe that the pattern of disease is well different, in fact 36 patients in placebo group were different from 26 and 29 present in the other 2 groups and EDSS score at entry group there were 25 less severe patients over 75 compared to 31 vs 69 and 30 vs 70.
No information about concealment allocation.
